note: X posts for the agentwright-cron worker. Each item is posted once at or after `at` (within 3 hours; later than that it is skipped and reported). The worker runs at :07 every hour, so the real posting time is the first :07 at or after `at` (`at` 02:30 goes out at 03:07). No post may really go out between 03:00 and 07:00 KST, so never set `at` between 02:08 and 06:07 KST; night slots are 23:00, 01:00 and 02:00 KST, one item per slot (two items due in the same hour go out an hour apart). No links unless the item is a click-now item (max 1 link post/day). Edit on main; no redeploy needed. Optional per item: community_id (numeric X Community id the account has joined; posted with share_with_followers, falls back to a normal post + alert if refused; max 1 community post/day, never the same text in two communities). Top-level "paused": true stops all posting (emergency stop for policy changes).

posts.text:
In a typical Claude Sonnet 5.5 request (4,000 tokens in, 600 out, 60% cached), output is 13% of the tokens and 64% of the cost.

If you want to cut your bill, look at max_tokens and answer length before you look at the prompt.

Claude Fable 5.2 costs $8 in / $40 out per million tokens, 2x Opus 5.5.

4,000 tokens in, 600 out, 60% cached:
Sonnet 5.5: $0.0094
Opus 5.5: $0.0189
Fable 5.2: $0.0373

Cache reads are $0.20/M on both Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5, so cache-heavy agents pay less than 2x.

Same request on Claude Sonnet 5.5, 4,000 tokens in and 600 out:

0% cache hits: $0.0140
60% cache hits: $0.0094

One cache_control line on the system prompt. It is the first thing to check before any pricing change.

A $20/month AI plan on Claude Sonnet 5.5, 300 requests per user: 76% margin.

The same user at 10x usage: -52%. Break-even is about 1,900 requests a month.

Run your own numbers in our free margin calculator (link in profile, under Tools).

If you recompute last month's LLM costs with today's price table, your totals move.

Store the rate used on every usage row, version the price table, and keep raw token counts so a re-price is a deliberate step.

Full write-up with code on our blog, link in profile.

The last line of defence most AI apps forget: a monthly spend limit on the API provider's side.

It is the only limit that still works when your own metering code has a bug.

Connecting MCP servers to your own Claude agent loop: one env variable for all servers, stdio and HTTP, namespaced tool names, an allowlist.

Plus the detail that costs money: keep tool order stable or your prompt cache misses.

On our blog, link in profile.

How our blog publishes every day without a daily deploy: each post is uploaded ahead of time, and a small Cloudflare Pages middleware returns 404 until the post's date arrives in Asia/Seoul time.

One deploy per batch of eight posts, nothing to run each morning.

We made a free remote MCP server for Claude API pricing.

Add https://agentwright.app/mcp to Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor and ask "what does this workload cost on Sonnet vs Haiku?" It knows caching and Batch API prices.

No sign-up, no key. Source is public.

Our Claude starter kit's agent loop is now public in full: 104 lines of TypeScript.

Streaming, parallel tool calls, a 12-turn limit, one cache breakpoint on the system prompt, and a plan-cap check before every model turn.

Read it before you write your own. Link in profile.

Not every Claude call has a user waiting: nightly digests, tagging, evals, backfills.

Send those through the Message Batches API and they cost half the standard price. Most batches finish within an hour, all within 24.

A 2M-token monthly cap can cost you $0.20 (all cache reads on Sonnet) or $40 (all output on Opus).

Cap each user's spend in dollars, not tokens, and reserve the worst case before the request so two parallel calls can't slip past.

Code on our blog, link in profile.

We opened sales for Agentwright Starter this week: the Next.js codebase behind the posts on this account, with metering, billing, auth and the agent loop already wired.

If you build on the Claude API, we'd like to hear what a kit like this is still missing. Link in profile.
